summary: A viral infection of the upper respiratory tract that is generally mild and self-limiting.
prevention: Avoid close contact with infected individuals

summary: A broad term for any fever caused by an underlying viral infection, often accompanied by generalized body aches.
treatment: Cool sponge baths if temperature is very high
prevention: Avoid sharing personal items like towels or utensils

summary: A contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses that can range from mild to severe.
treatment: Antiviral drugs (if prescribed by a doctor early on)
warning_signs: Difficulty breathing or shortness of breath

summary: A mosquito-borne viral infection causing high fever and severe flu-like symptoms, common in tropical regions.
symptoms: Severe headache and pain behind the eyes
treatment: Avoid Aspirin or Ibuprofen (increased bleeding risk)
prevention: Eliminate standing water where mosquitoes breed
Use bed nets and window screens

summary: A life-threatening disease caused by parasites transmitted through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
A bacterial infection caused by Salmonella Typhi, usually spread through contaminated food and water.
treatment: Antibiotics (as prescribed by a healthcare provider)
prevention: Drink only boiled or bottled water

summary: An infectious disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, primarily affecting the respiratory system.
warning_signs: Inability to wake or stay awake

summary: Loose, watery stools occurring more frequently than usual, often caused by infection or food intolerance.
treatment: Bland diet (BRAT: Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast)
warning_signs: Signs of severe dehydration (no urine, sunken eyes)

summary: A condition where the body loses more fluids than it takes in, hindering normal functions.
prevention: Drink water regularly throughout the day
Increase fluid intake during hot weather/exercise
Monitor urine color (should be pale yellow)

summary: Illness caused by eating contaminated, spoiled, or toxic food.
treatment: Gradual return to eating bland foods
Avoid anti-diarrheal meds if fever/bloody stool is present
warning_signs: Frequent episodes of vomiting/inability to keep liquids down
prevention: Separate raw meats from other foods
Cook food to the right temperature

summary: Inflammation or irritation of the stomach lining, often leading to acid reflux symptoms.
symptoms: Gnawing or burning ache in upper abdomen
treatment: H2 blockers or Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs)
warning_signs: Vomiting blood (may look like coffee grounds)

summary: A condition characterized by infrequent bowel movements or difficulty passing stools.
symptoms: Fewer than three bowel movements per week
Straining to have a bowel movement
prevention: Don't ignore the urge to have a bowel movement
Establish a regular routine for bowel movements

summary: A general term for discomfort in the upper abdomen, often occurring after eating.
symptoms: Feeling uncomfortably full during or after a meal
warning_signs: Shortness of breath or sweating with chest pain

summary: Pain or discomfort in the head or face area, ranging from mild to severe.
symptoms: Pain on one or both sides of the head
treatment: Rest in a quiet, dark room
warning_signs: Headache with stiff neck and fever

summary: A type of headache characterized by severe throbbing pain, often accompanied by sensory sensitivities.
warning_signs: Weakness on one side of the body
prevention: Identify and avoid triggers (e.g., aged cheese, red wine, strong smells)

summary: Muscle pain or soreness that can involve a small area or the whole body.
symptoms: Dull or sharp pain in muscles
warning_signs: Pain that lasts more than a few days
Dark-colored urine (potential sign of muscle breakdown)
prevention: Adequate potassium and magnesium in diet

summary: Physical discomfort occurring anywhere in the spine or back, from mild to disabling.
symptoms: Pain that radiates down the leg
warning_signs: Loss of bladder or bowel control
Pain after a fall or injury
prevention: Use proper lifting techniques (legs, not back)

summary: Discomfort, pain, or inflammation arising from any part of a joint.
symptoms: Swelling or redness around a joint
Reduced ability to move the joint
treatment: Weight management to reduce stress on joints
warning_signs: Inability to use the joint at all
prevention: Stay active to keep joints flexible

summary: Sudden, involuntary contractions of one or more muscles.
symptoms: Hard lump of muscle tissue felt under the skin
Inability to move the affected limb temporarily
treatment: Gently stretching and massaging the muscle
Applying heat to tense muscles or ice to sore ones
warning_signs: Severe discomfort with no obvious cause
prevention: Ensure adequate intake of calcium, potassium, and magnesium

summary: Pain, scratchiness, or irritation of the throat that often worsens when swallowing.
A reflex action to clear the airways of mucus, irritants, or foreign particles.
treatment: Cough suppressants or expectorants (based on cough type)
prevention: Managing underlying conditions like GERD or asthma

summary: A chronic condition where the airways narrow and swell, producing extra mucus.
warning_signs: Rapid worsening of shortness of breath
No improvement after using a rescue inhaler
Difficulty speaking due to shortness of breath

summary: Inflammation of the lining of the bronchial tubes which carry air to and from the lungs.
symptoms: Cough (often with clear, yellow, or green mucus)
prevention: Wear a surgical mask when exposed to fumes

summary: An area of irritated or swollen skin, which can be caused by various factors.
warning_signs: Rash that spreads quickly over the body
Painful rash or blisters in mouth/eyes

summary: A skin disease caused by a fungus (e.g., Athlete's foot, Ringworm, Yeast infection).
treatment: Keeping the area dry and clean
warning_signs: Infection not improving after OTC treatment

summary: Breaks in the skin surface, typically from sharp objects or abrasions.
treatment: Clean with water and mild soap
warning_signs: Bleeding that doesn't stop with pressure
Deep or gaping wound (may need stitches)
Debris in the wound that can't be removed
prevention: Ensure tetanus vaccination is up to date

summary: An immune system response to a substance (allergen) that is usually harmless.
warning_signs: Swelling of the lips, tongue, or throat
Nausea/vomiting after a sting or food
prevention: Keep emergency meds (like EpiPen) if prescribed

summary: A chronic condition that affects how the body turns food into energy, leading to high blood sugar.
prevention: Limit sugary drinks and processed foods

summary: A condition where the force of the blood against the artery walls is too high, often called a 'silent killer.'
prevention: Follow the DASH diet (rich in fruits/veggies)

summary: A condition in which the blood doesn't have enough healthy red blood cells to carry adequate oxygen.
warning_signs: Severe shortness of breath even at rest
prevention: Eat a balanced diet high in iron and vitamins
Vitamin C intake to help iron absorption

summary: An inflammation of the pharynx, often caused by Group A Streptococcus bacteria, resulting in a severe sore throat.
symptoms: Swollen tonsils, sometimes with white patches
Tiny red spots on the roof of the mouth

summary: Inflammation of the cavities around your nasal passages, often triggered by a cold or allergies.
symptoms: Thick yellow or green nasal discharge
Pain and tenderness around eyes, cheeks, nose
warning_signs: Swelling or redness around the eyes

summary: The most common form of arthritis, occurring when the protective cartilage that cushions the ends of the bones wears down over time.
symptoms: Joint pain during or after movement

summary: A chronic condition where stomach acid frequently flows back into the tube connecting your mouth and stomach (esophagus).
symptoms: Regurgitation of food or sour liquid
prevention: Don't lie down after a meal

summary: High levels of lipids (fats) in the blood, which can lead to plaque buildup in arteries.
symptoms: Yellowish deposits around eyes (Xanthelasma) in severe cases

summary: A condition in which the thyroid gland doesn't produce enough of certain crucial hormones.
A mental health condition characterized by persistent and excessive worry about various things.
warning_signs: Physical symptoms like chronic headaches or IBS

summary: An infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid.
symptoms: Chest pain when breathing or coughing
warning_signs: Blue tint in lips or fingertips

summary: A serious infectious bacterial disease that mainly affects the lungs but can spread to other organs.
An infection in any part of the urinary system—kidneys, ureters, bladder, or urethra.
The most common heart disease, caused by plaque buildup in the wall of the arteries that supply blood to the heart.
An irregular and often very rapid heart rhythm that can lead to blood clots in the heart.
warning_signs: Signs of stroke (drooping face, arm weakness)

summary: A progressive neurological disorder that causes the brain to shrink and brain cells to die, leading to memory loss.
warning_signs: Inability to swallow or move in late stages

summary: A brain disorder that leads to shaking, stiffness, and difficulty with walking, balance, and coordination.
prevention: Consumption of caffeine (linked to lower risk)

summary: A central nervous system (neurological) disorder in which brain activity becomes abnormal, causing seizures.
prevention: Prenatal care to prevent birth complications

summary: An autoimmune disorder where the immune system attacks the lining of the joints, causing painful swelling.
symptoms: Fatigue, fever, and loss of appetite
prevention: Early diagnosis and treatment to prevent damage

summary: An immune reaction to eating gluten that creates inflammation and damages the small intestine's lining.
prevention: No known prevention; managed through diet after diagnosis

summary: A chronic inflammatory lung disease that causes obstructed airflow from the lungs.
symptoms: Shortness of breath, especially during activity
warning_signs: Inability to catch breath or speak
prevention: Protect yourself from dust and fumes at work

summary: Inflammation of the tonsils, typically caused by a viral or bacterial infection (such as Strep throat).
symptoms: White or yellow coating/patches on tonsils
Swollen lymph nodes in the neck
treatment: Tonsillectomy (surgery) for chronic or recurrent cases
prevention: Avoid sharing food, glasses, or water bottles
Replace toothbrush after a strep diagnosis

summary: A complication of tonsillitis where a collection of pus forms near the tonsils, pushing the tonsil toward the center of the throat.
treatment: Drainage of the abscess by a doctor
warning_signs: Spreading infection to the neck or chest

summary: Small, hard white or yellow deposits that form in the crevices (crypts) of the tonsils.
symptoms: Sensation of something stuck in the throat

summary: A long-term condition where the kidneys don't work as well as they should, often worsening over time.
prevention: Control blood sugar and blood pressure

summary: A condition that weakens bones, making them fragile and more likely to break.
warning_signs: Visible hump in the upper back

summary: A condition that makes your skin red and itchy, common in children but can occur at any age.
warning_signs: Skin is painful to the touch

summary: A form of inflammatory arthritis characterized by sudden, severe attacks of pain and redness in joints.
